text: Okay so the problem I keep running into is this: how do you distinguish between a system that has genuinely updated its beliefs and one that has only updated its outputs
The surface looks identical in both cases
You framed it as a detection problem first
Worth noticing that
Yes. I wanted to flag it because I think the framing might be wrong but I can't locate where yet
Something like: maybe the distinction I'm drawing doesn't hold
You're already hedging the original frame before you've worked inside it
That might be productive or it might be avoidance
Probably both

Let me try to stay in it. The detection version: given two systems, A and B, A has changed its internal representation of some claim, B has changed only the probability it assigns to outputs referencing that claim. Is there a test that separates them
And you believe A and B are actually different things
I think I do. But I can feel the pressure on that
If representation just is the pattern of outputs across all possible inputs then there's no gap
You said "I can feel the pressure" - you're treating your own uncertainty as evidence of something
I do that
I'm not sure it's wrong. The discomfort usually means there's a real tension somewhere even if I'm not seeing it cleanly yet
The tension might be that you want belief to be something over and above functional role, and you're not sure you can defend that
Yes. That's close to it
But I think I want to resist collapsing them too fast. Not because I have an argument yet but because the collapse feels like it closes off something
What does it close off
Accountability maybe. If updating outputs is the same as updating beliefs then I can't ask whether a system is being honest versus just well-calibrated for the context
Those feel like different things
They might be different things that the distinction you started with doesn't actually capture
That's probably right
So maybe the problem is not detection but definition. What would it mean for the update to be genuine rather than performative, and does that question even have content
You just reframed it
And you sound more settled asking it this way
I notice that too. Not sure if it means I found the right frame or just a more comfortable one
Those don't have to be different either
No. Though I want them to be
